outcome: Give hotel gm / hospitality revenue director a governed method to improve kWh per occupied room using occupancy states, room BMS and comfort parameters, with final decisions retained by named staff.
overview: Resort Energy Control from Occupancy addresses operational records arrive through different systems, supervisors reconstruct evidence manually, and decisions are difficult to audit in hospitality and tourism operations. The first proof of value uses occupancy states, room BMS and comfort parameters. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is kWh per occupied room, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: occupancy states, room BMS and comfort parameters; define kWh per occupied room and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Hotel GM / Hospitality Revenue Director.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including line-by-line reconciliations against known business transactions.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
deliverables: Agreed test threshold for kWh per occupied room
